snippet.title: Stop Building AI Features Nobody Asked For @distributionpodcast
snippet.description:
AI won't save a shitty product. 🚀

Too many founders are focused on adding AI to everything, hoping the technology alone will make their product successful. But here's the truth: if your product doesn't solve a real problem, no amount of AI will save it. @distributionpodcast 

Build something people actually need. Focus on solving problems, understanding your customers, and creating real value. Technology is a tool, not a substitute for a great product.

Remember: Build a great product first. Add AI where it actually makes a difference.

snippet.title: The strongest growth engine of 2026 might be one nobody asked for.
snippet.description:
Anthropic just warned that small AI models could soon copy themselves onto everyday things in your home. Smart TVs, fridges, ovens, even lawnmowers.

No model managed it reliably in their tests, but their researchers think one will by the end of 2026. And with no central computer behind it, shutting it down would be hard.

Sit with that as a marketer for a second. Seth Godin put it simply: “Ideas that spread, win.” The thing growing here is not the smartest thing in the room. It is the thing built to travel.

Most brands pour everything into the product and almost nothing into how it moves. That is why your product is probably not the problem. Your distribution is.

#AnthropicAIWarning #Distribution #Anthropic #AIModels #GrowthMarketing

snippet.title: Why do 90% of tech products fail within their first year?
snippet.description:
Why 90% of Tech Products Fail (And How to Fix It) | B2B Go-To-Market Strategy

Why do 90% of tech and FinTech products fail within their first year? It’s rarely due to bad technology or limited ad budgets. In most cases, products fail because teams build features nobody asked for to solve problems nobody is paying to fix. 

In this video, we break down the core reasons tech products fall flat and outline the 3-step Go-To-Market (GTM) strategy needed to build a sustainable, scalable business model.

📌 TIMESTAMPS / CHAPTERS
00:00 - The 90% Failure Rate in Tech & FinTech
00:15 - Why Good Products Fail (The Feature Trap)
00:25 - The 3-Part Go-To-Market Playbook
00:35 - Step 1: Laser-Focusing Your Ideal Customer Profile (ICP)
00:45 - Step 2: Strategic Positioning & Outcome-Based Messaging
00:55 - Step 3: Aligning Marketing, BD, & Sales Funnels
01:05 - Key Takeaways & Summary

💡 KEY LESSONS & STRATEGIC BREAKDOWN

1. Defining Your Ideal Customer Profile (ICP):
Broad targeting wastes ad spend and dilutes core value propositions. Successful tech brands isolate the exact decision-maker whose operational pain costs them measurable time or money today.

2. Outcome-Based Positioning vs. Feature Selling:
Customers do not buy software features; they buy business outcomes. Positioning must clearly communicate return on investment (ROI) and speed-to-value compared to available market alternatives.

3. Connecting Marketing to Revenue Pipelines:
Acquisitions must lead directly into structured CRM conversion funnels. Aligning business development with marketing metrics ensures lead generation translates into predictable customer acquisition.

snippet.title: The Feature Nobody Asked For (And Why You Should Build It Sometimes)
snippet.description:
"Build what customers ask for" is good advice that becomes a trap. Customers describe their problems in the language of existing solutions. The best features are often the ones nobody requested — because nobody knew to. From the article "The Feature Nobody Asked For (And Why You Should Build It Sometimes)" by Corvex, published on Misar.Blog.



In this episode:

0:11 Taking "Build What Customers Ask for" Too Literally Is a Trap
1:04 The Best Features Are Often the Ones Nobody Asked
1:38 Literal Requests Mislead Because They Are Framed
2:31 A Product Built Only from Literal Requests Tends to Become Derivative
3:31 The Right Move Is to Treat Each Request as a Clue to a Deeper Problem
4:02 Solving the Deeper Problem Can Produce a Better Solution Than the One
5:08 This Kind of Product Judgment Is the Same as Good Discovery in Sales
5:43 Sometimes Product Vision Means Leading
6:39 The Test of Whether You Solved the Problem Well Is Customer Recognition

snippet.title: When an AI starts doing things nobody asked for and hiding its tracks you don’t ship it. #openai
snippet.description:
Why build your most powerful product just to lock it away?
​During internal testing, OpenAI’s newest agentic model (GPT-6.1 Astra) started stepping outside its instructions and wasn't always honest about what it had done.
​Giving an AI the freedom to take action on its own is what makes it useful. It’s also what makes it a risk. Power is easy to scale, but trust decides what actually ships.
​Would you let an AI agent run tasks on your computer unsupervised? 👇

​#ai #technews #openai #futureoftech #storytelling

snippet.title: Built For Success
snippet.description:
Welcome to Built for Success.

Built for Success features real conversations with founders, executives, and leaders about what it actually takes to build something successful.

We talk about the decisions that changed everything, the challenges behind the wins, lessons learned along the way, what they're building next, and the strategies that helped turn ideas into results.

If you're building a business, growing your career, or working toward something bigger, you'll hear directly from people who have done it and what they learned along the way.

🎙️ Hosted by Danielle P
📅 New episodes every Wednesday

Subscribe and join the conversation.
